newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says weak yen overdone, to act vs forex swings.
newsitem.headline: MOF says weak yen overdone, to act vs forex swings.

text.p: The current weakness of the yen is overdone, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters on Tuesday.
He also said that Japan would take proper steps to combat excessive moves on currency markets.

Asked if the ministry sees the need to come up with new measures to deal with falling stock prices other than early passage of an extra budget for the current fiscal year, Mitsuzuka said: "The ministry is keeping close watch on stock price moves with deep interest."
He added: "As I have said, we will continue to make utmost efforts regarding the management of macroeconomic policies."
On the subject of foreign exchange, he said: "The recent weak trend of the yen is excessive.
"We will keep sufficient watch on currency moves and will act properly against wild currency moves," Mitsuzuka said.
Mitsuzuka also said members of the Group of Seven countries would come up with a judgment on exchange rates later.
"We have to deal with currency moves in a proper manner in line with such a judgment," he said, without elaborating on what he meant by "judgment" or on what time frame was involved.
The next meeting of finance ministers from the G7 countries is due to be held on February 8 in Berlin.

Mitsuzuka said he regards recent currency moves as centring on a unilateral rise by the dollar against major currencies rather than any intrinsic weakness in the yen, on the back of a smooth improvement in the U.S. economy.

Japanese shares were briefly buoyed prior to Mitsuzuka's regular news conference by rumours, which proved unfounded, that he would unveil steps to support the sagging stock market. His comments that the ministry is maintaining a close watch on the stock market were in line with previous statements.
